purpose: This medicine is used to treat geographic atrophy (GA), which is an advanced form of dry age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Dry AMD is a condition where the center part of your retina slowly breaks down, affecting your central vision. Avacincaptad pegol helps slow down the growth of those damaged areas in your eye.
how_it_works: In people with geographic atrophy, a part of the body's immune system called the 'complement system' becomes overactive and damages the cells in the back of the eye. This medicine works by blocking a specific protein in that system called complement C5, which helps stop the chain reaction that damages your retina. Think of it like putting a lid on a process that's causing harm to your eye cells.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include eye discomfort, redness, or irritation after the injection. You may also notice blurry vision, small floating spots in your vision (floaters), or increased eye pressure. Some patients experience a feeling of something in the eye after the treatment.
warnings: There is a small risk of serious eye infections (endophthalmitis) or retinal detachment from the injection — tell your doctor right away if you have sudden vision changes, eye pain, or increased redness after treatment. This medicine may also increase the chance of developing the wet form of AMD, which is another type of macular degeneration. Let your doctor know about all eye conditions and medications before starting this treatment.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given as an injection directly into the eye by your eye doctor, once a month. The injection is done in a clinical setting and your eye will be numbed beforehand to keep you comfortable. Regular monthly visits are important to get the best results.
